questions.q: Where does an alerting rule like `CheckoutHighErrorRate` actually live?
options: In Alertmanager's own configuration file
On the Prometheus server, as a PromQL expression plus a condition
In Grafana's dashboard JSON
It doesn't need to be defined anywhere — Prometheus detects problems automatically
questions.explain: Alerting rules are defined on the Prometheus server itself (a PromQL expression plus a for duration). Alertmanager only receives alerts after the Prometheus server's rule evaluation decides one is firing.

questions.q: What does the `for: 5m` clause on an alerting rule do?
options: It deletes the alert after 5 minutes
It requires the condition to stay true for 5 straight minutes before the alert actually fires
It sets how often Alertmanager retries sending the notification
It groups alerts into 5-minute batches
questions.explain: The for duration prevents a brief, momentary blip from immediately paging someone — the underlying condition has to remain true continuously for that whole window first.

questions.q: Why does Alertmanager group alerts instead of forwarding each one individually?
options: Grouping is required by Prometheus's license
So that something like a bad deploy firing the same alert across a dozen pods produces one notification, not a dozen separate pages
Because Alertmanager can only send one notification per day
Grouping disables the alert instead of sending it
questions.explain: Without grouping, a single incident that triggers the same underlying alert across many instances would page someone once per instance. Grouping bundles alerts with similar labels into a single notification.

questions.q: What does a route in Alertmanager's configuration do?
options: It defines which PromQL query an alert rule uses
It sends alerts matching certain labels to a specific receiver, such as PagerDuty for critical alerts and Slack for the rest
It configures how the Prometheus server scrapes targets
It silences all alerts permanently
questions.explain: A route matches on an alert's labels (like severity or team) and determines which receiver — Slack, PagerDuty, email, etc. — the notification goes to.

questions.q: What is a silence in Alertmanager, and when would Northbridge use one?
options: A permanent change to an alerting rule's threshold
A temporary, time-bounded suppression of matching alerts, used for things like a planned deploy where the alert condition is expected and caused on purpose
A way to permanently disable Alertmanager
A setting that mutes Grafana dashboard panels
questions.explain: A silence mutes matching alerts for a set window without altering the underlying rule, and expires automatically — exactly the right tool for planned maintenance, like intentionally taking checkout down for a deploy.
